en: Theragāthā 1.9 Ekakanipāta, First Chapter The verse of the Elder Cūḷa-Panthaka: "Though they may speak of me as 'foolish' or 'stupid,' Or even as one who has lost his way, I shall not give way to anger; For I am one who has reached the end of birth. The verse of the Elder Mahā-Panthaka: "I have no teacher, nor do I have a rival; I am the Great Sage, the peerless one. Having abandoned all defilements, I dwell in peace, cooled and free from fever. The verse of the Elder Sīvali: "By what means did you cross the flood? How did you reach the further shore? Tell me, O monk, how you crossed over, And how you have attained the state of peace.
